title: Dental Calculus Field-Sampling Protocol
author: Susanna Sabin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bqecmtaw
materials: Replace top layer of your gloves.

steps.title: Put on protective gloves
steps.instruction: Wear two pairs of gloves; replace the outer pair after each sampling.

steps.title: Cover work surface with foil
steps.instruction: Lay two layers of aluminum foil on the work surface; replace the top layer after it contacts sampling debris or after each sample.

steps.title: Sterilize all utensils
steps.instruction: Wipe all utensils with alcohol wipes or with paper towels soaked in bleach (1:10 dilution with HPLC water). If bleach is used, rinse metal utensils with (preferably) HPLC water to prevent corrosion.

steps.title: Label collection tube
steps.instruction: Label the collection tube, keep it closed at all times before and after depositing the calculus sample to limit contamination.

steps.title: Complete metadata sheet
steps.instruction: Enter the tube ID and other required information on the metadata sheet.

steps.title: Label sample bags
steps.instruction: Label each bag with the corresponding tube ID for later storage.

steps.title: Prepare weighing paper
steps.instruction: Lay a fresh sheet of weighing paper, create a gentle crease to aid collection, and optionally place the paper inside a weighing boat or surround it with an aluminum‑foil barrier for better containment.

steps.title: Remove tooth and locate calculus
steps.instruction: If possible, remove the tooth from the jaw, locate the dental calculus deposit, avoid touching it, and check for fractures or weakened integrity; consult the collection curator if any damage is observed before proceeding.

steps.title: Write sample label on paper
steps.instruction: Write the sample name or tube label on a piece of paper and place this label next to the weighing paper.

steps.title: Position tooth and photograph
steps.instruction: Place the tooth on the weighing paper, photograph the whole tooth and the calculus from multiple angles (including close‑ups), include a scale if possible, and ensure the sample label is clearly visible.

steps.title: Record calculus location and condition
steps.instruction: On the metadata sheet, record the calculus deposit location (e.g., lingual, buccal), and note any evidence of disease, consolidants, or other relevant observations.

steps.title: Orient specimen for scraping
steps.instruction: Position the specimen so you can scrape the calculus with a downward motion toward the crease in the weighing paper.

steps.title: Scrape calculus with sterile scaler
steps.instruction: Using a sterile dental scaler, scrape the broad flat edge against the calculus deposit only (avoid enamel), moving downward toward the crease. Start with gentle pressure and increase if needed; if the deposit is powdery, scrape deeper into the bowl. Do not use the pick of the scaler.

steps.title: Transfer calculus to collection tube
steps.instruction: Gently tap the collected calculus from the weighing paper into the labelled tube, using the crease as a guide.

steps.title: Collect remaining calculus with forceps
steps.instruction: If any calculus remains on the paper, pick it up with sterile forceps or tweezers and place it directly into the tube.

steps.title: Seal tube and bag sample
steps.instruction: Close the tube cap securely and place the tube into its pre‑labelled sample bag.

steps.title: Sterilize utensils post‑sampling
steps.instruction: Wipe all used utensils again with alcohol wipes or bleach‑soaked paper towels; if bleach is used, rinse metal utensils with HPLC water to avoid corrosion.

steps.title: Photograph sampling site again
steps.instruction: Take another photograph of the tooth focusing on the sampling site, ensuring the sample ID remains visible.

steps.title: Record additional observations
steps.instruction: Add any further notes to the metadata sheet, such as an approximate weight of the calculus sample.

steps.title: Store tooth and clean workspace
steps.instruction: Return the tooth to appropriate storage, discard the weighing paper and weighing boat (if used), discard the top foil layer if necessary, and lay a fresh sheet of foil for the next sample.

steps.title: Replace gloves and continue sampling
steps.instruction: Replace the outer pair of gloves and repeat the sampling preparation starting at step 5.
